canonicalFacts.claim: Ulcerative colitis is a chronic inflammatory disease affecting the colon with rising worldwide incidence
The pathogenesis involves genetic predisposition, epithelial barrier defects, dysregulated immune responses, and environmental factors
Current treatments include 5-aminosalicylic acids, corticosteroids, immunosuppressants, and biologics with one-year clinical remission rates around 40%
Patients with ulcerative colitis have an increased risk of colorectal cancer, particularly with longer disease duration and greater anatomical extent
Concomitant 5-aminosalicylates provide no additional benefit in patients escalated to biologic therapy

redFlags: Acute severe ulcerative colitis is a medical emergency with high morbidity and mortality
Risk of colorectal cancer increases 8-10 years after UC diagnosis
Vedolizumab may rarely cause drug-induced liver injury
